app.name: Ember

app.confirmClose: An action is still running. Quit anyway?
app.linkBlocked: Link not opened (only https, mailto and softwarecenter are allowed): {url}
app.noUi: This exe was built without a user interface. Build the web UI first:
app.shortcutDescription: Ember – sets up your developer machine
app.uiRollback: UI {version} did not start in time. Ember goes back to the built-in version.
app.advancedOn: KI and Energy are visible now. Ctrl + E hides them again.

errors.proxyAuth: the proxy requires authentication, and Kerberos/NTLM with the Windows login did not work
errors.fixedProxyMissing: With "fixed proxy" a proxy (host:port) must be entered.
errors.proxyFormat: The proxy must be given as host:port, e.g. proxy.company.com:8080.
errors.portRange: The port must be between 1 and 65535.
errors.installDirMissing: Please enter an installation folder for px.
errors.installDirInvalid: The installation folder is not a valid path.
errors.localZipMissing: The local px zip was not found: {path}
errors.elevatedNoResult: The action with admin rights returned no result.
errors.elevationCancelled: The Windows prompt for admin rights was cancelled.
errors.gitIdentityInvalid: Please enter a name and a valid email address.
errors.llamaNoAsset: The current llama.cpp release has no Windows build "{variant}".
errors.llamaNoServer: llama-server.exe is missing from the downloaded archive.
errors.mailNoRecipient: The team configuration has no service center address (serviceCenter.email).
errors.modelUnknown: This model is not in the list.
errors.moduleNotAllowed: The advanced module is not enabled.
errors.noHttpClient: No network connection prepared – please start the installation from the beginning.
errors.pacMissing: px should use the PAC file, but none was found. Enter it in the settings or choose "fixed proxy".
errors.packageInvalid: "{package}" is not a valid npm package name.
errors.powerNoBackup: There is no saved previous state.
errors.powerProfileUnknown: The power profile "{id}" does not exist.
errors.powershellEmpty: PowerShell returned no data. The log shows what happened.
errors.powershellNoResult: PowerShell did not run the script ({way}: {detail}). A security policy may be blocking this call. The log has the details.
errors.proxyUnreachable: The proxy {proxy} cannot be reached via TCP. Are host and port correct, and does the firewall let Ember out?
errors.pxExeNotInZip: px.exe was not found in the archive.
errors.pxIniMissing: px did not write a px.ini: {path}
errors.pxNoWindowsZip: Release {tag} has no Windows zip. Available: {assets}
errors.pxPortTimeout: px is not listening on port {port} after {seconds} s. "Start px debug" shows the reason in the log.
errors.pxTestFailed: {detail} – "Start px debug" shows in the log what px is doing.
errors.refuseDelete: {path} is not deleted for safety reasons.
errors.refuseDeleteNoPx: {path} contains no px.exe and is therefore not deleted.
errors.releaseTagUnknown: Could not determine the current version of {repo}.
errors.sccmExecuteFailed: The Software Center client refused the installation (code {code}).
errors.sccmInstallFailed: According to Software Center the installation failed ({status}).
errors.sccmInstallTimeout: The installation has not finished after 45 minutes. Check "Installation status" in Software Center.
errors.softwareCenterMissing: Software Center cannot be opened. Is the Configuration Manager client installed?
errors.uiPackageInvalid: The downloaded UI package is invalid.
errors.webView2InstallFailed: WebView2 could not be installed (exit code {code}).
errors.webView2Signature: The signature of the WebView2 installer is invalid. For safety reasons it is not started.
errors.wolNoAnswer: {host} does not answer after 3 minutes. Is Wake-on-LAN enabled in the BIOS and on the network adapter?
errors.wolSendFailed: The magic packet could not be sent over any network connection.
errors.devToolDirectDisabled: According to the team configuration Ember does not install anything directly from the vendor. Ask the service center.
errors.devToolUnsigned: {file} has no valid signature. Ember deleted the file and installed nothing.
errors.devToolSigner: {file} is signed by “{signer}”, expected “{expected}”. Ember deleted the file and installed nothing.
errors.devToolNotFound: {tool} cannot be found after the installation. The log has the details.
errors.devToolNoRelease: No suitable version of {tool} was found.
errors.devToolNoChecksum: There is no checksum for {file}, so Ember does not install it.
errors.nodeInUse: Node.js is in use right now ({path}). Close all terminals and editors that use node and try again.
errors.certsNone: No valid certificate was found in the Windows certificate store.
errors.playwrightNoNode: Node.js with npm is missing. Install it above under Developer tools.
errors.playwrightNotInProject: The project in {path} does not use Playwright. Add it with “npm install -D @playwright/test”.
errors.playwrightNoBrowsers: After the installation there are no browsers in {path}.
errors.playwrightCertificates: The download failed on the certificate: the company proxy inspects TLS and Node.js does not know the company certificate. Set up “Node.js certificates” under Proxy → Diagnosis and try again.
errors.playwrightProxyAuth: The proxy asks for authentication (407). Is px running? The Proxy page shows its status; without px, npx and Playwright do not get through.
errors.playwrightBlocked: The download server cannot be reached or is blocked. Is px running? Otherwise cdn.playwright.dev is probably blocked: ask for an internal mirror in the team configuration (playwright.downloadHost) or test with Edge (channel: 'msedge').

jobs.failedAt: Failed at "{step}" – details at the step and in the log

net.pacFailed: PAC file could not be loaded: {detail}
net.githubRateLimit: GitHub API limit reached, Ember falls back to the release web page.

start.title: Hello {name}
start.subtitle: This is how your machine is doing

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.subtitle: px signs in at the company proxy with Kerberos using your Windows login. Your tools only talk to {url}, no passwords needed anywhere.

px.title: px proxy
px.debugRunning: px is running in debug mode · {url}
px.portClosed: px is running, but the port is not open yet
px.outdated: The px configuration no longer matches the settings (e.g. a new proxy in the team configuration). "Install / update" brings it up to date.
px.confirmUninstall: px will be stopped, autostart removed, the proxy entries of environment variables, git, npm, NuGet, pip and VS Code reverted and the installation folder deleted. Entries that do not point to px stay unchanged.
px.debugHint: In debug mode px runs in its own console window with verbose output. Ember also writes it to C:\Ember\Logs and opens that folder when px debug ends.

diag.title: Diagnosis
diag.subtitle: Which tool uses which proxy?
diag.kerberosNote: npm, pip and most Node, Python, Go and Rust tools cannot do Kerberos. That is why they point to px, and px handles the sign-in.

hints.windows: Stays unchanged: px reads exactly this setting to find the company proxy.
hints.nuget: dotnet restore and Visual Studio read http_proxy from %APPDATA%\NuGet\NuGet.Config.
hints.vscode: Ember only changes "http.proxy" in settings.json; comments and other entries stay.
hints.nodeCerts: Node.js, npm, npx and Playwright do not use the Windows certificate store. If the company proxy inspects TLS, downloads fail with “unable to get local issuer certificate”. “Set up” exports the trusted certificates from Windows to C:\Ember\Certs and sets NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.

proxy.keptForeign: Not set by Ember, left unchanged: {value}

detect.atStart: Company proxy detected at start: PAC {pac}, proxy {proxy}. These values apply as long as neither you nor the team configuration sets something else.
detect.nothing: No company proxy detected at start (no PAC address, no system proxy).

nodeCerts.done: Exported {count} certificates from Windows to {path}; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is set. Applies to newly opened terminals.

px.title: px
px.saveHung: px did not exit after --save, but px.ini was written.
px.autostartOk: px now starts automatically at login
px.debugStarted: px is running in debug mode in its own window. The output is also written to {file}.
px.debugWindow: px debug is running. The output is also written to {file}. Close this window or click “Stop px debug” in Ember to end it.

git.title: Git identity
git.subtitle: Name and email for your commits. Ember suggests them from your Windows account and only saves after you confirm.
git.name: Name
git.confirm: Set git config --global user.name "{name}" and user.email "{email}"?
git.gitMissing: git is not installed on this machine. Get it from Software Center.

software.title: Software
software.subtitle: Developer tools, Playwright browsers and everything Software Center offers.
software.noClient: No Software Center client found. Installing then only works through the service center.
software.empty: The team configuration does not list any programs yet (section "software").
software.confirmInstall: Install "{name}" through Software Center? This is the same as "Install" in Software Center.

steps.trigger: Start the installation in Software Center

software.triggered: Software Center has taken over the installation.
software.centerHint: Everything Software Center offers on this machine. Installing runs through the Configuration Manager client, with your IT's approvals.
software.nothingOffered: Software Center offers nothing to this machine right now.

mail.title: Message to the service center
mail.subtitle: Ember prepares the mail. You review it and send it yourself.
mail.resultOutlook: The draft is open in Outlook with the report attached.
mail.resultMailto: Your mail program is open. The report is in the clipboard and saved as a file – please attach it.
mail.noServiceCenter: No service center address is configured yet (team.json → serviceCenter.email).

softwareRequest.subject: Software request: {app} for {user}

adminAction.subject: Admin rights needed on {computer}

problem.subject: Problem on {computer}

power.title: Power
power.subtitle: Ember only changes values inside the "{scheme}" scheme. It never switches the power plan and never creates "High performance" or "Ultimate performance".
power.notActive: The active plan is not "{scheme}". Changes only take effect once it is active.
power.schemeByPolicy: The active plan is set by group policy.
power.confirmApply: Apply the profile "{name}"? Ember saves the current values first.
power.confirmDefaults: Reset all values of "{name}" to the factory settings?

ai-performance.name: AI performance (plugged in)
ai-performance.description: Full CPU power for local models and builds while plugged in: aggressive boost, energy performance preference 0 for all core classes, 5–100 % clock. Battery settings stay unchanged.

sleep-ac.name: No sleep when plugged in
sleep-ac.description: When plugged in the machine does not sleep or hibernate; the display turns off after 15 minutes. Long builds and downloads keep running.

lid-ac.name: Lid & power button
lid-ac.description: On the dock, closing the lid does nothing; the power button shuts down.

wol.title: Wake-on-LAN for this machine
wol.subtitle: So this machine can be woken up from shut down. The target state comes from a machine where it already works.
wol.macHint: Enter this MAC as wake target in the AI tab on the other machine.
wol.fastStartupOff: off (right for waking from shut down)
wol.fastStartupOn: on – prevents waking from shut down
wol.noAdapters: No wired network adapter found. Wake-on-LAN only works via cable (also through the dock).
wol.confirmApply: Set the Wake-on-LAN settings? Windows asks for admin rights, and the network connection drops briefly.
wol.confirmReset: Reset the adapter settings to the driver defaults and turn fast startup back on?
wol.biosHint: Ember cannot check the BIOS. On Dell: turn on "Wake on LAN", "Wake on Dell USB-C Dock" and possibly "MAC Address Pass-Through", and turn off "Deep Sleep Control".

system.title: System & policies
system.subtitle: Ember cannot change group policies. It shows what applies, refreshes them and sets up the things you are allowed to change yourself.

gpo.title: Group policies (user)
gpo.timeout: gpresult did not answer within {seconds} s. “Update policies now” often helps; check again afterwards.

devMode.title: Windows developer mode
devMode.hint: For information only. You can turn it on in Windows settings under "For developers", if allowed.

ai.title: AI
ai.subtitle: Enable Wake-on-LAN for this machine, manage llama.cpp and models, run llama-server.

gpu.title: Graphics card
gpu.none: No NVIDIA graphics card found (nvidia-smi missing).
gpu.readOnly: Display only – Ember does not change power limits.

models.title: Models
models.empty: No models entered yet. Add a GGUF download address, e.g. from Hugging Face.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Saved in {path}
settings.loadFailed: Settings could not be read, Ember uses the defaults: {detail}

team.title: Team configuration
team.description: A shared team.json on a network share provides internal domains, software list, admins, service center address and mail templates. When something changes there, Ember picks it up at the next start. Ember detects the company proxy itself.
team.fromCache: Network share not reachable ({error}) – Ember uses the local copy of {date}.
team.none: No team configuration set up yet.

source.file: from ember-team.txt next to the exe

proxy.title: Company proxy
proxy.upstreamHint: Also used for downloads as long as px is not running yet. Empty = Windows system proxy.
proxy.notDetected: No proxy settings found. Please enter them manually.
proxy.autoHint: Ember detects the company proxy from Windows at every start (PAC address, proxy from the PAC file, system proxy). Only enter something if the detection is wrong.

px.title: px
px.localZip: Local px zip instead of download (optional)

tools.title: Tools to switch during px installation

advanced.title: Advanced modules
advanced.admin: You are listed as an admin in the team configuration. Ctrl + E shows and hides the KI and Energy tabs.
advanced.notAdmin: KI and Energy are only available to admins listed in the team configuration (team.json → admins).

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: You can also switch colour scheme and design at the bottom of the sidebar. Ivy has a green sidebar, Ember a warm reddish ground; both with ivy.

log.title: Log
log.subtitle: Everything Ember does. Each session is also written to {path}.

update.uiReadyText: Version {version} has been downloaded. Reloading takes a second; Ember stays open.
update.exeReadyText: For this update Ember restarts once, briefly.
update.checked: Update check: latest version {latest}, installed {current}, UI {ui}

team.fromCache: Team configuration {path} not reachable ({detail}), using local copy of {date}
team.failed: Team configuration {path} could not be loaded: {detail}

install.prerelease: Test build {version}: Ember runs portable, without copying itself to C:\Ember\App and without automatic updates.
install.notSingleFile: Not a single-file build: Ember runs from its current location.
install.newerInstalled: C:\Ember\App already contains the newer version {version} – Ember starts that one.
install.noRights: No write access to {path}: {detail} – Ember runs from its current location.
install.locked: Copy to {path} not possible ({detail}). Is Ember already running there? Ember runs from its current location for now.
install.failed: Self-copy failed: {detail} – Ember runs from its current location.
install.shortcutFailed: Start menu entry could not be created: {detail}

webview2.title: Setting up Ember
webview2.preparing: The user interface needs Microsoft WebView2. Ember fetches it once …
webview2.missing: WebView2 runtime missing – Ember downloads it.

devtools.title: Developer tools
devtools.subtitle: The basics for development. If your IT offers a tool in Software Center, Ember installs it from there. Otherwise it comes straight from the vendor through px, with checked checksum and signature.

nodejs.description: JavaScript runtime with npm. Ember puts it under C:\Ember\Tools\node for your account, no admin rights needed.

git.description: git with Git Bash and Credential Manager, for your account without admin rights.

vscode.description: Microsoft's editor as a user installation, no admin rights needed.

python.description: Current Python 3 with pip and the py launcher, for your account.

visualstudio.description: Visual Studio Professional with the .NET desktop and ASP.NET workloads. Needs admin rights and a license; you sign in yourself afterwards.

dotnet.description: Current .NET SDK with long-term support (LTS) for dotnet build and dotnet run. Needs admin rights.

pwsh.description: PowerShell 7 next to Windows PowerShell 5.1. Needs admin rights.

devtools.uacHint: Windows will ask for admin rights in a moment.
devtools.reboot: Installed. A restart completes the installation.
devtools.nodeReady: Node.js is in {path}. Newly opened terminals find node and npm through PATH.
devtools.pathAdded: Added to PATH: {dirs}. Applies to newly opened terminals.
devtools.visualstudioHint: The Visual Studio installer downloads the workloads itself. Depending on the connection this takes 20 to 60 minutes.
devtools.confirmInstall: Install {name}? Ember downloads the installer through px, checks it and installs. Close the program first if it is already running.
devtools.confirmMany: Install these tools: {names}. For Visual Studio, .NET SDK and PowerShell 7 Windows asks for admin rights.

bruno.description: API client like Postman, without an account; collections live as files in the repo. For your account, no admin rights needed.

devtools.unsigned: not signed, checksum from GitHub matches

playwright.title: Playwright browsers
playwright.subtitle: Playwright belongs to the project; its browsers live in a shared cache. Ember installs exactly the browsers your project's Playwright version needs, through px and with the company certificates.
playwright.noProject: Choose the folder with your project's package.json.
playwright.foundWanted: {package} {wanted} according to package.json, npm install still to do
playwright.notInProject: package.json lists no Playwright (@playwright/test or playwright).
playwright.cacheEmpty: No browsers in the cache yet.
playwright.certsMissing: Node.js does not know the company certificates yet. If the download stops with a certificate error, set up “Node.js certificates” under Proxy → Diagnosis.
playwright.edgeText: Microsoft Edge is installed on every Windows machine. With this setting Playwright tests in Edge, and Chromium tests need no browser download:
